intro.0: A small step up. You will make a few tiny objects that work together - one asks another for what it needs, each one has a single job, and a class uses the tool it is handed. Nothing new to learn - just good habits you will use again soon.
task.1.title: Two objects talk to each other
task.1.context: A `Greeter` does not know what time it is. So it [[concept:pr-collaboration|asks a `Clock` and uses the answer]] to choose a hello. The example below asks a `Sensor` - do the same thing with the clock.
task.1.goal.0: Ask the `clock` for the hour. Before 12, return `"Good morning"`. Otherwise return `"Good afternoon"`.
task.1.goal.1: This clock says 9, so it should print Good morning.
task.2.title: Ask another object for the price
task.2.context:
A `Cart` should not keep prices - the `PriceList` knows those. So the cart [[concept:pr-delegation|asks the price list for a price]] and times it by how many you want. First keep the price list you are handed, then ask it.

The example below asks a `Catalog` - do the same with the price list.
task.2.goal.0: Save the `prices` you get in the constructor, then return the item's price times `qty`.
task.2.goal.1: A book is 10 and qty is 3, so the output should be 30.
task.3.title: A method that does one thing
task.3.context: A good method does [[concept:pr-single-responsibility|just one thing]] you can name. `Area` does one sum - the two sides times each other - and nothing else. The example below is one job for a box - do the same for the rectangle.
task.3.goal.0: Return the area of the rectangle - `width` times `height`.
task.3.goal.1: For 4 by 5 the output should be 20.
task.4.title: Give each job its own class
task.4.context:
`Checkout` was doing two jobs at once: the maths (price times how many) and the words (turning that number into text). Two jobs in one place means two reasons it might need to change.

Move the words into `ReceiptFormatter`. `Checkout` keeps the maths and asks the formatter for the text. The example below splits a sale the same way.
task.4.goal.0: Give `ReceiptFormatter` a `Format(int total)` that returns `"Total: "` and then the total.
task.4.goal.1: In `Pay`, make a formatter and ask it for the text. For 10 by 2 the output should be Total: 20.
task.5.title: Use what is handed in
task.5.context:
A class does not need to make its own tools. `Mailer` is handed an `Outbox` in its constructor and uses that one - it never does `new Outbox()` itself. A tool handed in from outside is easy to swap later.

The example below hands a `Printer` its `Ink` - do the same with the mailer and its outbox.
task.5.goal.0: Keep the `outbox` you are handed in the constructor, then send `"hello "` and then `who` through it.
task.5.goal.1: For Sam the output should be sent: hello Sam.
task.6.title: Wire two objects and run
task.6.context:
Now put it all together: a `Worker` is handed a `ConsoleLog` and reports through it. Keep the log, then let `Report` write the status through the log it was given. Two small objects helping each other is the shape of most real code.

The example below wires a `Bell` to a `Speaker` - do the same with the worker and its log.
task.6.goal.0: Keep the `log` you are handed in the constructor, then write the `status` through it in `Report`.
task.6.goal.1: `Main` reports work done, so the output should be work done.
task.7.title: What you learned
task.7.summaryIntro: You read and wrote a few small objects that work together. These are the habits the SOLID drills will use next.
task.7.summaryItems.0.title: Objects help each other -
task.7.summaryItems.0.text: one object asks another for what it needs, then uses the answer.
task.7.summaryItems.1.title: One job per method -
task.7.summaryItems.1.text: a method that does exactly one thing is easy to name and trust.
task.7.summaryItems.2.title: Split the jobs up -
task.7.summaryItems.2.text: when a method does two things, give one of them its own class or method.
task.7.summaryItems.3.title: Use what you are given -
task.7.summaryItems.3.text: let a class take its tool through the constructor, so it is easy to swap later.
task.7.summaryItems.4.title: Wire it up and run -
task.7.summaryItems.4.text: make the parts, hand them in, and let them talk - the shape of most real code.
task.7.summaryClose: Next you will meet these ideas by their real names in the design track: single responsibility, and using what is handed in.
